Two mistakes in the customization, on top of the default behaviour. By default Argo CD refreshes an Application every time a resource it tracks changes; your FinOps job changes 2,400 tracked KafkaTopics every five minutes, which is the refresh storm in the log.

1. resource.ignoreResourceUpdatesEnabled: "false" turns ignoring of resource updates off, so no ignoreResourceUpdates rule is used. Remove the key or set it to "true" (the default).
2. The pointer is wrong: in a JSON pointer a '/' inside a key must be written as ~1. Use

data:
  resource.customizations.ignoreResourceUpdates.kafka.strimzi.io_KafkaTopic: |
    jsonPointers:
    - /metadata/annotations/finops.example.com~1bytes-last-hour

This only tells the controller not to refresh on changes to that field. It does not change diffing, so changes to spec in Git or in the cluster are still detected.

Check: in the application-controller log the 'Requesting app refresh caused by object update' lines for kind=KafkaTopic should stop and, at debug log level, 'Ignoring change of object because none of the watched resource fields have changed' should appear. CPU should fall within minutes.

Do not raise timeout.reconciliation (that is Git polling) and do not take the topics out of Argo CD: pruning or deleting the KafkaTopics makes the Topic Operator delete the topics.

Fix the flag first: resource.ignoreResourceUpdatesEnabled: "false" disables every ignore-updates rule, so remove it (the default is true). Then express the path with jq, which avoids pointer escaping:

resource.customizations.ignoreResourceUpdates.kafka.strimzi.io_KafkaTopic: |
  jqPathExpressions:
  - '.metadata.annotations."finops.example.com/bytes-last-hour"'

Why: every update of a tracked resource refreshes its Application by default; with the rule active the controller skips updates that only touch that annotation. If you prefer, the same jq expression can go into a system-level ignoreDifferences customization for the KafkaTopic kind, because Argo CD adds system-level ignoreDifferences to the ignored updates by default. Confirm with the controller's debug-level log line 'Ignoring change of object because none of the watched resource fields have changed'. Drift detection on spec is unaffected.

value: Argo CD 3.6.1. One ApplicationSet deploys our Strimzi 1.3.1 Kafka platform (operator, Kafka cluster, topics) to five clusters registered in Argo CD with an env label: dev, staging, prod-eu and prod-us (both env=prod) and dr (env=dr). After a bad Kafka upgrade hit every cluster at once, I added a RollingSync strategy so changes go to dev, then staging, then the prod clusters one at a time. I applied it yesterday and changed the Kafka version in Git this morning: all five clusters synced at once again. argocd-cmd-params-cm has no applicationsetcontroller.* keys. What is wrong, and once fixed, what will happen to each cluster on the next change?

value:
Two things keep RollingSync from working.

1. The feature is off. Progressive syncs must be enabled in the ApplicationSet controller; your argocd-cmd-params-cm does not set applicationsetcontroller.enable.progressive.syncs: "true", so the strategy was not applied and each Application's automated policy synced as soon as Git changed. Set it to "true" (or pass --enable-progressive-syncs / ARGOCD_APPLICATIONSET_CONTROLLER_ENABLE_PROGRESSIVE_SYNCS=true) and restart the ApplicationSet controller.
2. The steps match labels on the generated Applications, not on the cluster Secrets. Your template sets none, so no step would select anything. Add:

  template:
    metadata:
      name: 'kafka-platform-{{.name}}'
      labels:
        env: '{{index .metadata.labels "env"}}'

What happens next time:
- dev syncs first; the controller waits until it is Healthy;
- then staging, again until Healthy;
- then prod: maxUpdate: 1 updates prod-eu and prod-us one at a time;
- dr matches no step: it is excluded from the rolling sync and stays OutOfSync until someone syncs it from the CLI or UI. Add a fourth step for dr if it should follow prod.

Also expect RollingSync to force autosync off on the generated Applications (the controller logs warnings for the automated block); selfHeal no longer acts by itself and syncs come from the rollout.

Two things are wrong with the RBAC, and the error shows both: the request comes from system:serviceaccount:data:etl-connect and goes to the namespace db-credentials.
1. Strimzi runs the Connect pods with the service account <KafkaConnect name>-connect, here etl-connect. Your RoleBinding names a service account etl, which the pods do not use.
2. You applied the Role and RoleBinding in data. The provider reads the Secret through the Kubernetes API in the Secret's own namespace, so the access rights must be granted in db-credentials; a RoleBinding only gives rights within its namespace. The Secret can stay where it is.
Fix (least access): in db-credentials, a Role with apiGroups [""], resources [secrets], resourceNames [orders-mysql], verbs [get], and a RoleBinding to ServiceAccount etl-connect in namespace data. Delete the useless pair in data.
Check before retrying: create a SubjectAccessReview (authorization.k8s.io/v1) with spec.user system:serviceaccount:data:etl-connect and spec.resourceAttributes namespace db-credentials, verb get, resource secrets, name orders-mysql; status.allowed must be true.
Then restart the failed connector: kubectl annotate kafkaconnector orders-cdc -n data strimzi.io/restart="true" (or "includeTasks,onlyFailed"), and check that READY becomes True and the task is RUNNING. The other four connectors are not touched.
Do not grant cluster-wide read on secrets, do not mount the Secret (it cannot be mounted across namespaces anyway) and do not paste the password into the connector.

Do not run five operators. The Strimzi CRDs and ClusterRoles are cluster-scoped, so several Cluster Operators conflict even in separate namespaces, and mixing 1.2.0 and 1.3.1 makes it worse: one set of CRDs serves everyone. Run one Cluster Operator for the Kubernetes cluster, in its own namespace, owned by the platform team.
- Watch: all namespaces (or label the team namespaces and watch all); a long list of namespaces is the slowest option.
- One Kafka cluster per namespace: staging and prod of a team go into two namespaces (team-a-staging, team-a-prod), which also gives clean names, access and recovery.
- Team control: install strimzi-admin and strimzi-view; they aggregate into admin, edit and view, so each team manages its own Kafka, KafkaNodePool, KafkaTopic and KafkaUser resources in its namespaces without cluster-wide rights.
- Independence: Strimzi upgrades become one central change, announced and tested first on a staging Kubernetes cluster. Teams keep control of their Kafka version: spec.kafka.version per cluster, any version the operator supports (Strimzi 1.3.1: 4.2.0 to 4.3.2), and they choose when to roll it. value:
Main problem: group.id has no effect in Kafka Streams. The consumer group is the application.id, invoice-agg-v2, so invoice-consumer's committed offsets are not used. invoice-agg-v2 has no offsets, and Kafka Streams defaults auto.offset.reset to earliest (not latest as plain consumers do), so the first start would re-read 90 days of invoices.

Switch-over: stop invoice-consumer at 22:00, then give the new group exactly the old group's positions before the first start. Export them with
kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server ... --reset-offsets --group invoice-consumer --all-topics --to-current --export > offsets.csv
(without --execute this changes nothing) and apply them with
kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server ... --reset-offsets --group invoice-agg-v2 --from-file offsets.csv --execute
or with kafka-streams-application-reset.sh --application-id invoice-agg-v2 --input-topics invoices and --from-file with a CSV of those offsets, first with --dry-run. A --to-datetime reset is safe only with a time before the oldest invoice invoice-consumer had not processed yet; the stop time itself can skip invoices if the old service had lag. Alternatively, keep the old offsets by setting application.id=invoice-consumer.

- replication.factor=1 creates single-replica changelog and repartition topics; below 3 exactly-once is effectively void. Use replication.factor=3 (or -1 with a broker default of 3) and topic.min.insync.replicas=2.
- Remove group.id to avoid confusion.
